knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Incorrect gradient computation for zero-length target sequences in sequence-loss functions
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Loss functions that reduce over variable-length target sequences may rely on hidden assumptions about target length positivity. When zero-length targets are present, gradient normalization or reduction can become incorrect.

risk_dimensions.shape: Batched variable-length target sequences with one or more zero-length targets; log_probs shapes where the target dimension can be empty for selected batch elements; interactions between time, batch, and class dimensions when some targets are empty.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Backward pass requested after forward propagation with zero-length targets; autograd graph contains a loss value derived from empty target sequences.

failure_mechanism.description: The loss implementation may not correctly handle zero-length target sequences during gradient computation. Hidden assumptions about target length positivity can affect reduction or normalization logic, leading to incorrect gradients.

input_exploration: Explore batches containing one or more zero-length target sequences
Vary the number and position of empty targets within a batch
Explore all-empty target batches versus partially empty target batches
Explore valid log_probs shapes combined with empty target cases
constraint_awareness: Ensure per-sample target lengths remain within valid input sequence bounds
Treat zero-length target sequences as valid boundary inputs
Keep alignment and reduction constraints of sequence losses satisfied while introducing empty targets
oracle_strategy: Compare gradients against a finite-difference or reference implementation
Monitor for inconsistent or unexpected gradient values
Use tolerance-based comparisons for floating-point gradients

transferability.reason: The principle applies to sequence loss or reduction APIs that accept per-sample lengths or variable-length targets and compute gradients. APIs with zero-length or degenerate sequence dimensions may share this failure mode, while APIs with fixed-length targets are less likely to be affected.

important_considerations: Probe zero-length and degenerate target/length dimensions for sequence loss functions
Focus on backward gradient correctness, not just forward loss values
Explore batched inputs with varying target lengths and empty sequences
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that mutate target lengths to include zero-length targets while preserving shape and length validity, then compare backward gradients against a numerical reference.
